summary.tagline: A historic mosaic of ancient woodland, rolling ridges, and hidden valleys across Kent, Sussex, and Surrey.

travel.headline: Check Local Attraction Closures and Event Schedules
travel.reservation: Entry to the High Weald is generally unrestricted as it is a lived-in landscape, though specific nature reserves or historic attractions within the area may suggest or require advance booking. Visitors should check individual manager websites for the most current updates on access to specific sites.

days.title: Ancient Forest and Ridges

stops.name: Ashdown Forest
stops.detail: Explore an open area of the National Landscape characterized by its unique sandstone and clay geography, offering a contrast to the dense surrounding woods.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for transit between forest tracks and valley villages; conditions vary.
days.note: The terrain is hilly and broken; pace your visit to allow for self-guided walks on uneven ground.

intel.title: Village and Trailhead Access
intel.text: Evidence does not specify parking capacity or fee structures; verify local arrangements in gateway towns or at forest trailheads before arrival.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: The remote nature of the ridges and valleys may impact mobile reception. Download self-guided walk maps from official sources before entering deeper valley areas.

intel.title: Local Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available in surrounding gateway cities like Hastings, but availability within the rural interior is not confirmed by current evidence.

intel.title: Seasonal Planning
intel.text: The landscape is a patchwork of fields and woods that changes significantly with the seasons. Spring and fall offer the most distinct colors in the shaws and ancient woodlands.

intel.title: Public Rights of Way
intel.text: The area is accessible via an extensive network of self-guided walks across Kent, Sussex, and Surrey. Stick to marked paths to respect local producers and nature reserves.

plan.arrival: Collect a rental in Tunbridge Wells or Hastings, then head toward the central ridges to begin exploring the historic sandstone dome.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the paved rural roads, though narrow lanes require cautious driving.
plan.goldenHour: The ridges overlooking the Rother Valley offer expansive views, though specific sunset times vary by season.
